belief: “I’ve already messed things up, so there is no point in stopping now.”
belief_plain: I’ve already messed things up, so there is no point in stopping now
origins: “I’ve already messed things up, so there is no point in stopping now” is hopelessness wearing the clothes of realism. The past may be genuinely damaged: trust, health, money, time, relationships. None of that is brushed aside here. The lie is the conclusion that more harm is the logical next step, and that mercy is no longer on offer. Stopping still matters on the worst day. It matters because you are still alive, and because God’s mercies are new in the morning, not only in the years before things went wrong. If this belief includes wanting to die, please reach for help now. You do not have to decide the rest of your life today. If you want help, call the SAMHSA National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357. Do not try to stop or withdraw on your own if that could make you sick. A doctor can help you do it safely, and a counselor can walk with you. Needing that help is not a failure. If you are thinking about ending your life, call or text 988 in the United States, or tell someone near you right away.
self: I have already ruined it, so more does not matter.
Mercy is for people who stopped sooner.
There is no point in a doctor now.
replacement: What I have done is not the end of the story. God’s mercy is new today, and stopping still matters.
